instruction: I want a niche product recommendation website where I can curate lists of tech gadgets, home goods, and fitness products, each with brief reviews and affiliate purchase links. I should be able to create, edit, categorize, and tag product entries, and mark certain items as featured on the homepage. Visitors should be able to browse products by category, sort and filter them by attributes like price range or rating, and search by keyword. Each product should have its own detail page showing my review, key specs, and a clear button linking to the external retailer.

checklist.content: An administrator can create and edit products in any supported category, including their name, price, rating, brief description, full review, image, retailer link, tags, specifications, and featured status; saved changes are immediately reflected in product browsing and detail views.
Marking or unmarking a product as featured updates the homepage featured collection, and visitors can browse the complete set of featured products.
checklist.bug: The homepage renders only the first three featured products, so a fourth marked product is omitted. The destination intended to expose the complete featured set uses ?featured=true, but the products page ignores that parameter and displays all products.

checklist.content: Keyword search matches product names, brief descriptions, and tags case-insensitively, and displays only matching products with an accurate result count.
A tag newly assigned to an existing product becomes available as a tag-filter choice and selecting it returns the matching product.
checklist.bug: Edited tags are stored on the product and work in keyword search, but the filter choices come from the static initial-product tag list, so newly assigned tags never appear as selectable filters.

checklist.content: When creating a product, an administrator can assign one or more new tag values, and the saved tags appear on the product and participate in keyword search.
An administrator can add, rename, or remove tags on an existing product, and the saved tag set is reflected on the product detail page and in keyword search.
An administrator can assign a product to exactly one supported category, and the product appears under the selected category after saving.
Visitors can filter the complete product list by Tech Gadgets, Home Goods, or Fitness, and the visible products and result count update to match the selected category.
Visitors can browse the complete product list, where every product exposes its name, category, price, rating, brief review, image, and a purchase action.
Visitors can sort products by newest, top rating, ascending price, or descending price, and can filter them by a price range or minimum rating.
Every product belongs to exactly one of the three supported categories: Tech Gadgets, Home Goods, or Fitness.
Every displayed result satisfies all active search, category, price, and rating criteria; when multiple tags are selected, each result has at least one selected tag.
Changing a search, filter, or sort criterion updates the product set, order, and result count without requiring a manual page reload.
Selecting a product's image or name opens the detail page for that same product.
Each product's purchase action opens the corresponding product page on an external retailer website.
checklist.bug: All seeded affiliate links point to example.com documentation placeholders, such as https://example.com/sony-xm5, rather than actual retailer product pages.

checklist.content: For every complete product record, the detail page displays the matching name, category, rating, price, brief description, full review, tags, key specifications, image, and retailer action.
Every seeded product uses relevant category and tag values, and those values remain consistent between browsing and detail views.

A product's name, category, price, rating, and brief description remain consistent across homepage, category, list, and detail views, while the detail view presents its complete review and specifications without truncation.
Product additions and edits remain available after the page is reloaded or revisited in a later session.
checklist.bug: Products are held only in React component state. Reloading the page recreates the initial product list and discards every admin addition or edit.

checklist.content: A product cannot be published until it has the content needed for a usable recommendation, including a name, supported category, non-negative price, rating from 0 to 5, brief description, full review, image, valid external retailer link, and at least one complete specification.
checklist.bug: The form validates only name and brief description. It accepts a product with a blank image, retailer link, review, and specifications and a zero price, producing an incomplete detail page with an empty purchase destination.

checklist.content: Whenever category filtering is offered, choosing a different category updates both the active category and the displayed products.
checklist.bug: On a category page, the category selector offers all categories but its change handler immediately overwrites every selection with the route's original category, so choosing another category has no effect.

checklist.content: An invalid product or category identifier shows a clear not-found state and does not display unrelated product data.

instruction: I want a job board webpage where employers can create and manage job listings by entering details like title, description, location, salary range, and required skills. Job seekers should be able to browse all available listings, filter them by industry, location, and employment type, and search by keywords. Each job listing page should display full details and allow job seekers to submit a simple application form with their contact information and a short message. There should also be a basic dashboard for employers to view their posted jobs and see a list of submitted applications for each listing.

checklist.content: Employers can publish a job listing with a title, industry, employment type, location, valid salary range, description, and required skills; the new listing appears in the employer dashboard and the job-seeker listing.
Employers can delete one of their posted jobs only after confirming the action; the job and its applications are then removed from the employer dashboard and the job-seeker listing.
The employer dashboard lists all active jobs posted by the current employer and shows accurate active-job and total-application counts.
The employer dashboard lets the employer open each posted job's application list and view the applications associated with that job.
Job seekers can browse the complete list of available jobs see an accurate result count and open any listing to view its details.
Job seekers can filter listings by industry, location, and employment type individually or in combination; clearing the criteria restores the full list.
Keyword search matches job titles, company names, and required skills without case sensitivity and immediately updates the visible results and count.
On a job details page, a job seeker can submit an application with a name, syntactically valid email address, optional phone number, and message and receives a clear success confirmation.
A job application cannot be submitted when the required name email or message is missing or when the email syntax is invalid; the invalid field is identified to the user.

A job cannot be published until its title, industry, employment type, location, description, salary range, and at least one required skill are provided; the salary values must be non-negative with the minimum no greater than the maximum, and invalid data produces clear feedback.
checklist.bug: The form publishes jobs with no industry, employment type, location, or skills and accepts a minimum salary greater than the maximum, producing incomplete or inverted listings without a validation message.

checklist.content: A job seeker cannot submit another application for the same job using an email address already used for that job; the existing application remains unchanged.
checklist.bug: The same name and email can be submitted repeatedly for one job and every duplicate is added to that job's application list.

checklist.content: A successfully submitted application produces visible confirmation and appears exactly once under the matching job in the employer dashboard with the submitted information.
Changing search or filter criteria immediately refreshes the matching jobs and result count including the no-results state; clearing all criteria restores the full list.
Every job card displays the job title, company, industry, employment type, location, salary range, posting date, and required skills.
A job details page displays information matching the selected listing: title, company, industry, employment type, location, salary range, posting date, full description, and required skills.
For each application, the employer can view the applicant's name, email address, optional phone number, message, and submission date as a distinct record.
Employers can edit the details of a published job and the updated information is reflected in both employer and job-seeker views.
checklist.bug: Published jobs have no edit action or edit route and the job state exposes no update operation.

checklist.content: Published jobs, submitted applications, and job deletions remain in effect after the page is reloaded.
checklist.bug: All changes exist only in React component memory; reloading restores the original seeded jobs and applications and reverses any in-session changes.

checklist.content: Newly published jobs and newly submitted applications display an accurate submission date relative to the user's current date.
checklist.bug: Records created today are displayed as "Yesterday" because the relative-date calculation rounds any positive same-day elapsed interval up to one full day.

instruction: I want a wedding planning website where couples can create and update a simple planning dashboard with key details like wedding date, budget, and guest count. They should be able to browse, filter, and search venue and vendor listings by categories such as location type, price range, and service type, and mark favorites for later. The site should also offer a collection of planning tips and checklists that users can view, save to their dashboard, and mark as completed.

checklist.content: Couples can create their locally saved wedding dashboard by entering both partner names, a future wedding date, a positive budget, and a non-negative whole-number guest count; the saved values are shown on the dashboard.
Couples can reopen their wedding details, change any saved partner name, date, budget, or guest count, save the changes, and see the updated values on the dashboard.
Users can filter venues by venue type and price range and vendors by service type and price range, individually or in combination; clearing the criteria restores the full corresponding list.
Keyword search matches relevant venue and vendor information, including names, descriptions, locations, and vendor specialties, without case sensitivity and updates the visible results and count.
Users can add or remove any venue or vendor from their favorites and view the current favorite venues and vendors together in the saved-favorites area.
Users can browse planning checklists by category, open a checklist, and view every task with its explanatory guidance.
Users can save or unsave a whole planning checklist and the dashboard updates its saved-checklist count and preview accordingly.
The dashboard accepts only a positive numeric wedding budget; zero, negative, empty, or otherwise invalid values are rejected without replacing the previously saved budget.
checklist.bug: The dashboard saves zero or negative budgets because wedding details are stored without validation.

checklist.content: The dashboard accepts only a non-negative whole-number guest count; negative or fractional values are rejected without replacing the previously saved count.
checklist.bug: The dashboard saves negative and fractional guest counts because wedding details are stored without validation.

checklist.content: Favorite venues, favorite vendors, and saved checklists remain available after navigating away and after reloading the application.
A saved wedding date must be a valid future calendar date; current or past dates are rejected without replacing the previously saved date.
checklist.bug: The date field and save action have no future-date validation, so a non-future date can be saved.

checklist.content: Users can open any venue or vendor listing to view its complete details.
checklist.bug: Venue "View Details" and vendor "View Profile" actions have no handlers, and the application defines no listing-detail routes.

checklist.content: Users can mark and unmark checklist tasks; the checklist percentage updates immediately, aggregate dashboard progress updates accordingly, and completion state remains after reload.
Visible venue or vendor results and their count update immediately as search or filter criteria change, without a separate submit action; clearing all criteria restores the full list.

After valid wedding details are saved, the dashboard displays the couple's names, formatted wedding date, budget, guest count, planning progress, favorite counts or previews, and saved-checklist counts or previews.
Each venue and vendor listing presents its name, location, category or service type, price range, rating, and summary; venues also show guest capacity and vendors show offered specialties.
The checklist collection covers planning, ceremony, reception, attire, and honeymoon topics, with at least one checklist per category and a title and explanatory description for every task.

When search and filter criteria are combined, every visible result satisfies all active criteria, the displayed result count is accurate, a clear no-match state appears for zero results, and clearing restores the full list.
If a user changes wedding details and selects Cancel, the saved dashboard values remain unchanged and reopening the editor shows the last saved values rather than the cancelled draft.
checklist.bug: Cancel only closes the editor; it does not reset the draft, so cancelled values reappear when the editor is reopened.

instruction: I want a resume-building webpage where users can create and edit professional resumes using pre-designed templates. Users should be able to enter and organize their information (such as contact details, work experience, education, and skills), choose a template style, and customize basic layout options like section order and headings. The page should let users preview their resume, duplicate or rename versions, and save multiple variations for different job applications. Users should also be able to quickly search and filter their saved resumes by title or date created.

checklist.content: Users can create a new resume with blank contact, summary, experience, education, and skills content and begin editing it immediately.
Users can choose among the Modern, Classic, and Minimal resume styles; changing the style updates the preview without losing the resume's content.
Users can enter and edit contact details and a professional summary, add, edit, remove, and reorder work and education entries, and add, change, or remove skills.
Users can change the order of resume sections and hide or show individual sections, and the preview reflects the resulting layout.
Users can view the active resume in a preview, hide the preview, and show it again without losing editor content or the selected template.
Users can duplicate an existing resume, give the copy a different title, and edit the copy without changing the source resume.
Users can create and manage multiple distinct resume variations for different applications during the current session.
Users can search saved resumes by title without case sensitivity and order the results by creation date from newest to oldest or oldest to newest; clearing the search restores all resumes.
For each past work or education entry, the end month must not precede the start month and neither date may be in the future; invalid periods are rejected with clear feedback.
checklist.bug: Work and education date fields have no past-date bounds or cross-field validation. In August 2026, the runtime accepted a work entry starting in December 2035 and ending in January 2030 and displayed it in the preview without feedback.

checklist.content: Experience and education dates use a consistent month/year format, and marking a work position as current clears and disables its end date.
Created, edited, duplicated, renamed, and deleted resume versions remain unchanged after the application is reloaded.
checklist.bug: Resume state is kept only in React component memory. Reloading discards all in-session changes and restores the original three seeded resumes.

checklist.content: Changes to resume fields and the selected template appear in the visible preview immediately, without requiring a manual save or refresh.
Changing a section's order or visibility updates the preview immediately and preserves the new layout while navigating within the current session.

Resume edits are retained automatically when the user moves between editor areas, returns to the dashboard, and reopens the resume during the current session; the dashboard reflects that the resume was updated.
For the selected style, the preview renders every visible section that has content and keeps the complete resume readable through scrolling when it exceeds the available preview area.

Contact details, summary, work experience, education, and skills entered for a resume remain present when switching editor areas, returning to the dashboard, and reopening that resume during the current session.
After a resume is duplicated, editing any content in the copy does not alter the corresponding content in the original, and editing the original does not alter the copy.
After a resume is renamed, the same non-empty title is shown in its editor and on its dashboard card.
Users can narrow saved resumes by an exact creation date or a creation-date range and clear the date criterion to restore all matching titles.
checklist.bug: The dashboard exposes title search and creation-date sorting only; it has no creation-date search or filter control. Searching for a displayed date produces no results.

checklist.content: Every section heading that the editor allows the user to customize is shown with that customized text in each resume style where the section is visible.
checklist.bug: The contact-section title is never rendered by any template, and the Minimal template renders summary content without its editable summary heading, so those exposed heading changes have no effect in the preview.

checklist.content: A resume cannot be renamed to an empty or whitespace-only title; the current title remains and the user receives clear validation feedback.
checklist.bug: The dashboard rename dialog accepts an empty value and saves a blank resume title with no validation message.

instruction: I want a web-based bookkeeping application where users can track income and expenses, categorize transactions, and view summarized reports such as monthly profit and loss. Users should be able to create and manage simple financial records (like invoices, bills, and payments) and assign them to customizable categories or accounts. The site should provide basic tools to review and adjust entries, filter records by date or category, and see simple dashboards of their financial status. It should also allow users to mark items as tax-related and generate a basic tax summary they can review and print.

checklist.content: Users can create financial transactions with a type, date, description, amount, and category, and may also record a reference, notes, and tax-related status.
Users can view a summary of their financial status, including total balance, current-month income and expenses, net profit or loss, financial trends, spending by category, and recent transactions.
Users can search transactions by keywords contained in their descriptions or references.
Users can review an annual tax summary containing taxable income, deductible expenses, net taxable income, category breakdowns, and the corresponding tax-related transactions.
Users can filter financial transactions by income or expense type, category, and date range.
A valid newly created transaction is retained and shown with the date, description, category, reference, amount, and tax-related status supplied by the user.
Users can update or delete existing financial transactions, and the resulting records reflect those changes.
Users can create, edit, and delete income or expense categories, including the category name, type, and color.
The categories available for a transaction are compatible with its income or expense type, and the assigned category is retained with the transaction.
Users can mark or unmark a transaction as tax-related when creating or updating it.
When search, type, category, and date criteria are combined, every resulting transaction satisfies all active criteria; removing the criteria restores the full set of transactions.
Financial transactions without a description or amount cannot be created, and the missing required information is identified to the user.
A transaction date range whose start date is later than its end date must be rejected with an explanation of the invalid range.
checklist.bug: The app accepts an inverted date range without feedback and can present a misleading empty result.

checklist.content: Within the current session, adding, updating, or deleting a current-month transaction immediately updates the corresponding financial summaries, reports, and recent activity.
Marking or unmarking a transaction as tax-related updates its recorded tax status and its inclusion in the corresponding annual tax summary.
The transaction count and total amount for each category update when categorized transactions are created or changed.
Users can print the tax summary for a selected year without an application error.
Users can view each transaction's date, description, category, reference, amount, and tax-related status, together with income and expense totals for the current result set.
Current-month income, expenses, net profit or loss, recent activity, and monthly report totals accurately reflect the underlying transactions.
When a financial chart represents a non-zero amount, its axis labels must use enough precision to distinguish that amount from zero, including for values below $500.
checklist.bug: Non-zero values below $500 are plotted, but every axis label is displayed as '$0k', making the chart misleading.

checklist.content: Financial transactions without an assigned category cannot be created, and a missing category is identified to the user.
checklist.bug: The app accepts transactions without a category; they appear without a category in transaction records and as 'Unknown' in tax summaries.

checklist.content: Deleting a category assigned to existing transactions must be blocked or require reassignment so no transaction is left with a blank or Unknown category.
checklist.bug: The app deletes assigned categories without checking or reassigning their transactions, leaving those transactions uncategorized and reports showing 'Unknown'.

instruction: I want a web application where users can browse a list of restaurants, view details such as cuisine type and average price, and select a date, time, and party size to reserve a table. The site should let users create and manage their reservations, including viewing upcoming bookings and canceling or modifying them. Users should also be able to submit simple reviews and ratings for restaurants they have visited, and optionally apply basic discount coupons during the reservation process.

checklist.content: Users can browse restaurants and view each restaurant's name, cuisine, average price per diner, rating, location, description, and notable dining features.
checklist.bug: The app shows symbolic price tiers such as '$$$$' but provides no average price per diner.

checklist.content: Users can search restaurants by name, cuisine, or neighborhood and can combine the search with cuisine and price-range filters; every displayed restaurant satisfies all active criteria.

Users can create a reservation by selecting a future date, an available time, and a party size, providing the required contact information, and submitting it; a successful booking is confirmed and appears among upcoming reservations with the supplied details.

Users can view their upcoming reservations and cancel one after confirming the action; the cancelled reservation is removed from upcoming reservations and retained with a cancelled status in reservation history.
Users can submit a one-to-five-star rating, visit date, name, and written review for a restaurant, and the new review is retained and displayed only with that restaurant.
During reservation, users can apply a supported coupon, see the offered discount, remove it if desired, and have the applied coupon recorded with the resulting reservation.
Past dates are unavailable for new reservations, while a valid future date can be combined with one of the restaurant's available reservation times.
Users can change the date, time, and party size of an upcoming reservation, and the reservation list retains and displays all submitted changes.
checklist.bug: The modification flow can change time and party size but provides no way to change the reservation date.

checklist.content: A review can be submitted only for a restaurant covered by the user's completed reservation, and each completed reservation can authorize at most one review.
checklist.bug: Review submission is not linked to reservations or user identity, so anyone can review any restaurant repeatedly without a completed visit.

checklist.content: A coupon is accepted only while all of its stated eligibility conditions are met, including first-reservation, day, and party-size rules, and no reservation can have more than one coupon applied.
checklist.bug: Coupon eligibility is only checked for minimum party size at application time: WEEKEND20 applies on weekdays, WELCOME10 is not limited to a first reservation, and GROUP15 remains applied after reducing the party below six.

checklist.content: A reservation cannot be created without a date, time, guest name, valid email address, and phone number, and the missing or invalid information is identified to the user.
For an upcoming reservation, users can open its modification choices and save supported changes, while cancellation requires an explicit confirmation before taking effect.
Creating, modifying, or canceling a reservation produces immediate visible confirmation, and the reservation views reflect the new state in the same session without a manual reload.
Users can distinguish upcoming reservations from past or cancelled reservations and can view each reservation's restaurant, date, time, party size, status, location, and applied coupon when present.
A restaurant's displayed rating and review count remain consistent between the restaurant list and its details, and submitting a review updates every displayed summary derived from those reviews.
checklist.bug: The list shows The Golden Fork as 4.8 with 312 reviews, while its detail page immediately shows 4.5 with 2 reviews; locally submitted reviews affect only the detail summary, leaving the list stale.

instruction: I want a community forum where users can register, create profiles with a short bio and interests, start and reply to discussion threads in different categories, and upvote or like helpful posts. People should be able to search for threads by keywords, filter by category, and see a list of trending or most active discussions over a recent period.

checklist.content: A visitor can register a unique username and email with a password of at least six characters, is signed in as the new user, and can sign out and sign back in with the same credentials during the current session; duplicate usernames or emails are rejected.
A registered user can edit their bio and comma-separated interests, save the changes, and see the saved bio and interests on their own public profile.
A logged-in user can publish a discussion with a category, title, and body; the published discussion displays those values and appears in its selected category.
A logged-in user can add a non-empty reply to a discussion, and the reply appears without a manual reload while the discussion's displayed reply total increases by one.
A logged-in user can add or remove their single upvote on another user's discussion or reply, and the displayed count and selected state update immediately.
Submitting a keyword search returns only discussions whose title or body contains the keyword, case-insensitively, and an unmatched keyword produces an empty result with clear feedback.
checklist.bug: The visible search field accepts a query, but submitting it leaves the unfiltered discussion list on screen.

checklist.content: Selecting a discussion category shows only discussions assigned to that category, and selecting a different category changes the result set to that category.
The Most Active discussion list is ordered by reply count from highest to lowest and updates its order when reply activity changes the ranking.
From a discussion or reply, users can open the author's public profile and view the username, bio, interests, join date, reputation, and authored discussions.
Within the same loaded session, a user's saved profile details, authored discussions, replies, and vote state remain intact after logging out and logging back in.
A discussion cannot be published without a category, non-blank title, and non-blank body; the missing information is identified and no discussion is created.
The Trending discussion list is ordered by upvote count from highest to lowest and updates its order when voting changes the ranking.
An account can be signed in only with its registered password, and an incorrect password is rejected without creating a logged-in session.
checklist.bug: Login looks up only the email address and ignores the supplied password, so any non-empty password signs in to an existing account.

checklist.content: Registered accounts, signed-in status, profile changes, authored discussions, replies, and vote state survive a page reload and remain available when the user returns.
checklist.bug: All users, authentication, discussions, replies, profile edits, and votes are held only in React memory and reset to seed data on reload.

checklist.content: Every discussion's displayed reply total matches the number of replies listed on its detail view, and adding a reply keeps both totals consistent.
checklist.bug: Seeded discussions report large reply totals that do not match their reply lists; for example, one discussion shows 67 replies but lists only one, then changes to 68 versus two after a new reply.

checklist.content: Trending and most-active views that describe recent popularity use a stated recent time window and rank discussions only by interactions within that window.
checklist.bug: The app has no recent-activity window and ranks all seeded discussions by all-time upvotes or reply counts, even when every displayed discussion is more than two years old.

checklist.content: Category and community counts accurately reflect the discussions, replies, and members available in the forum and update when those records are created.
checklist.bug: Category and community counts are hard-coded and contradict the available data; for example, Technology is labelled with 243 discussions while its category page contains two, and creating content does not update the counters.

checklist.content: An unauthenticated user who attempts to start a discussion is taken to a usable sign-in screen and can return to discussion creation after authenticating.
checklist.bug: Opening the new-discussion route while signed out renders only an empty notifications region and neither redirects to nor displays the sign-in screen.

instruction: I want a marketplace website dedicated to second-hand and upcycled products where users can register, create listings with photos, descriptions, prices, and locations, and where others can search, filter, and sort items by category, price range, condition, and distance. Buyers should be able to add items to a simple cart or send a purchase request, and sellers should be able to update or remove their listings when items are no longer available.

checklist.content: Sellers can create a listing by attaching one or more of their own product photos and supplying a title, description, non-negative price, category, condition, location, and upcycled status; the created listing retains and displays the submitted information.
checklist.bug: The listing form has no photo upload or URL input and can only attach up to four fixed stock images.

checklist.content: Sellers can edit the title, description, photos, price, category, condition, location, and upcycled status of an existing listing they own, and the saved listing displays the changes.
checklist.bug: Owned listings can be viewed, marked sold or available, or deleted, but there is no way to edit their details.

checklist.content: Sellers can mark an owned listing as sold or available and can delete it after confirmation; their listing view immediately reflects the resulting status or removal.
A listing marked sold or deleted is no longer offered to buyers in browse results and cannot be newly added to a cart or used to start a purchase request.
A user can register with a name, unique valid email address, password of at least six characters, and location; successful registration is confirmed and leaves the new user signed in.

Buyers can combine category, minimum and maximum price, condition, distance, and upcycled-only filters and sort the available listings by newest, price, or distance; every result satisfies all active criteria.
checklist.bug: The price control exposes only the minimum-price thumb, so buyers cannot set a maximum price. In addition, newly created listings have no computed distance and are treated as zero miles away, causing them to pass every distance limit.

checklist.content: Buyers can search available listings case-insensitively by words in the title, description, or location; every result matches the query, and clearing it restores the unsearched result set.
A signed-in buyer can add an available listing they do not own to the cart; the item is retained once with its title, photo, location, and price, and the cart total is correct.
A signed-in buyer can submit a non-empty purchase-request message for an available listing they do not own and receives visible confirmation that it was submitted.
A login attempt using an email that is not registered is rejected and does not create an authenticated session.
Registration rejects an email already used by an account, including a case-only variation, without replacing the existing account.
A registered account can be authenticated only with its correct password; an incorrect password is rejected without creating a signed-in session.
checklist.bug: Login ignores the password and authenticates any registered email with any non-empty password; registration does not retain passwords for later verification.

checklist.content: Seller-management actions are available only for listings owned by the signed-in seller and are not exposed when that user views another seller's listing.
A listing cannot be created without at least one photo, a title, description, valid price, category, condition, and location, and the missing required information is identified to the seller.
A listing price must be a finite number greater than or equal to zero; negative or non-numeric prices are rejected without creating the listing.
Attempting to register an existing email produces immediate, visible duplicate-account feedback and keeps the registration form available for correction.
Search results and the available-item count update as the buyer types or clears a query, without requiring a separate search submission.
Changing any available filter or sort choice immediately updates the displayed listings and result count, and clearing all filters restores the unfiltered available listings.
Adding a listing to the cart produces immediate visible confirmation and updates the cart count, line item, and total without a manual reload.
Each listing's details present its photos, title, description, price, category, condition, location, seller, listing date, availability, and upcycled status consistently with the listing data.
Choosing a category from the category-browsing page opens browse results containing only available listings in that category and shows a matching result count.
checklist.bug: Category choices navigate with a category query parameter, but the browse page never reads it and displays all available listings.

checklist.content: After a buyer submits a purchase request, the relevant seller can view the requested item and buyer message, and a cart request is reported as sent only after a request has been recorded for each cart item.
checklist.bug: There is no seller-facing purchase-request view. The cart action shows success and clears the cart without recording any purchase requests.

checklist.content: Creating or managing listings, adding items to or viewing the cart, and submitting purchase requests require a signed-in account; unauthenticated attempts are blocked with a clear sign-in prompt or redirect.

instruction: I want a to-do webpage where I can add tasks with titles, optional descriptions, and deadlines, then edit, complete, or delete them. I’d like to mark tasks as completed without losing them entirely, and have an easy way to view active tasks first. The page should also let me assign a simple priority to each task and sort my list by that priority or by deadline.It supports binding one or more prerequisite dependent tasks to any task. If Task A is dependent on Task B, the edit and complete buttons of Task A will be grayed out when Task B is not yet completed, with only the description and priority fields available for modification. Meanwhile, a prominent label stating "Prerequisite Task B Incomplete" will be displayed next to Task A. The system also enables visual connection of dependent tasks via dashed lines, and hovering over the connection will trigger a pop-up window showing the details of the dependency chain.

checklist.content: Users can sort the tasks in the current view by priority, with high-priority tasks before medium-priority tasks and medium-priority tasks before low-priority tasks.
Users can sort the tasks in the current view by deadline, with the earliest deadlines first and tasks without deadlines after dated tasks.
When a task is blocked by an incomplete prerequisite, users can still change its description and priority, but cannot change its title or deadline.
checklist.bug: Blocked tasks have no usable edit action, so their description and priority cannot be changed.

checklist.content: Users can create a task with a non-empty title; the new task is retained in the active list and the active-task count increases.
When creating a task, users can provide a title, optional description, optional deadline, priority, and zero or more prerequisites, and the created task retains the submitted details.
Users can update an unblocked task's title, description, deadline, priority, and prerequisites, and can delete a task; saved changes are retained and a deleted task is removed from the task views.
Users can mark an eligible active task as completed; it leaves the active view, appears in the completed view, and the active and completed counts update.
Users can switch between active and completed task views; each view shows only tasks in the corresponding state and displays the corresponding count.
Users can assign one or more existing tasks as prerequisites of another task, and the saved task retains and displays the resulting dependency state.
A task with any incomplete prerequisite is visibly distinguished as blocked, and its completion action remains unavailable until all prerequisites are complete.
A blocked task displays a prominent warning that names its single incomplete prerequisite or reports the number of incomplete prerequisites when there are several.
A task cannot be marked completed while any prerequisite is incomplete; after all prerequisites are completed, it becomes eligible for completion.
Users cannot create a direct or indirect circular dependency between tasks; any task whose selection would create a cycle is unavailable as a prerequisite.
A new task cannot be created from an empty or whitespace-only title, and attempting to do so leaves the task list unchanged.
Completing a task does not delete it: it remains available in the completed view until the user reopens or deletes it.
Hovering over a visual connection between dependent tasks displays the related dependency chain and the completion state of its tasks.
checklist.bug: Hovering the dashed dependency connection does not display the dependency-chain pop-up.

checklist.content: Hovering over a blocked task's prerequisite warning displays the dependency chain and identifies which prerequisite tasks are still pending.
Each task displays its title and priority, displays its description and deadline when supplied, exposes any blocking prerequisite state, and visibly distinguishes completed tasks from active tasks.

Reopening a prerequisite of a completed dependent task cannot leave that dependent task simultaneously completed and blocked; the system either prevents the prerequisite from being reopened or returns affected dependents to a valid incomplete state.
checklist.bug: A prerequisite can be reopened after its dependent is completed, leaving the dependent in the completed view with an incomplete-prerequisite warning and disabled completion control.

instruction: I want a technical specifications knowledge base where engineers can browse technical documents organized by modules. Each document should display its title, content sections, and any related documents it references. Users should be able to navigate between related documents through clickable links and collapse or expand content sections to make reading easier.An additional advanced function is dynamic knowledge graph visualization for document relationships, which visually maps connections between modules, documents and key knowledge points with interactive nodes and links for intuitive navigation.It is divided into the tabs of Document View, Graph and Favorites; the previously adjusted page states (e.g., whether paragraphs are collapsed or expanded, the zoom level of the graph) must be retained when switching tabs. Paragraphs must be expanded before their links can be clicked, and the page shall display a prompt if a link is clicked prematurely. Document information shall be displayed synchronously across different tabs. Favorite content is stored locally, with a real-time count of favorites maintained; favorite markers shall not be lost after filtering and sorting. The page must show corresponding prompts for scenarios such as no documents found and invalid links.

checklist.content: The document list identifies each document's module; choosing a module shows only documents from that module, and choosing all modules restores the complete list.
Selecting a document displays its title, description, version and update date, content sections, and related documents.
From an expanded content section or the related-documents list, choosing a valid document reference makes the referenced document the visible document.
Collapsing an expanded content section hides that section's body and expanded reference links while leaving the section available to reopen.
Expanding a collapsed content section restores that section's body and any reference links it contains.
Users can select a knowledge-graph node and receive a visible selection indication, and can change the graph zoom and reset the graph view with visible zoom feedback.
The knowledge graph represents every available document across all modules and their related-document connections, and its view controls allow the complete graph to be brought into view.
The application provides Documents, Knowledge Graph, and Favorites views, and users can switch among all three.
Switching among Documents, Knowledge Graph, and Favorites preserves the selected document, each section's expanded or collapsed state, and the graph's zoom and pan state.

Favorites are retained after reload, their navigation count updates immediately, their markers survive document filtering and sorting, and the Favorites view continues to expose every favorited document regardless of a module filter used in Documents.
checklist.bug: A module filter selected in Documents remains active but hidden in Favorites, so favorited documents from other modules disappear from the Favorites list even though the count still includes them.

checklist.content: A document never lists itself as either a content-section reference or a related document.
The knowledge graph contains one node for every available document, associates each node with the document's module, and draws connections for the available related-document relationships.
Each content section has a clear collapsed or expanded indicator, and the indicator's state agrees with whether the section body and expanded links are visible.
Choosing a document node in the knowledge graph opens that document in the document view without requiring a separate tab change, while preserving the graph view for later return.
checklist.bug: Choosing a graph node only highlights it and records the selection; the application remains on the graph until the user manually switches to Documents.

checklist.content: Choosing a reference link shown for a collapsed section leaves the current document open and displays a prompt to expand the section; after expansion, choosing the same link opens its target document.
When search or module criteria match no documents, the document list displays a clear no-results message, and clearing those criteria restores matching documents.

instruction:
I want a website that implements a pure front-end immersive browsing experience for Chinese intangible cultural heritage. The homepage contains multiple lists of heritage projects, and clicking on any project opens a rotatable 360° panorama scene, where each hotspot corresponds to a specific heritage project (such as traditional crafts, folk activities, or performing arts). Users can drag to rotate the view, zoom in and out, and click any hotspot to open an information overlay displaying the title, images, origin region, and a brief description. The overlay includes a “View Details” link, which navigates to a dedicated detail page showing the full introduction and multiple images. When users return from the detail page, the page must restore the 360° view and the corresponding hotspot to the state it was in before entering the detail page.
The panoramic perspective and anchor point positions are calculated in real time and must not pause even when the scene is zoomed. The lists support filtering and sorting, the panoramic scene allows drag-and-drop rotation and zooming, and the detail pages enable image browsing—all operational states are preserved after any action. The page must display corresponding prompts for scenarios such as slow panoramic loading, unloaded anchor points, and failed image loading on detail pages.

checklist.content: Users can view the complete list of heritage items, together with an accurate visible result count.

Selecting a loaded hotspot in the panorama opens a usable information overlay for the matching heritage item, including its title, image, category, region, brief description, and an action to view full details.
checklist.bug: The hotspot overlay is displaced down and right, leaving most content and actions outside the viewport. Framer Motion's inline transform overrides the centering transform classes.

checklist.content: A heritage detail page presents the matching title, full introduction, category, region, inclusion year when available, and a gallery containing multiple images.
Users can search the heritage list, filter it by any supported category or region, and sort it by name, year, or region; the displayed items and result count update accordingly.
After visiting a heritage detail page and returning to the panorama, the previous camera orientation and zoom level are restored.
Every displayed heritage item belongs to one supported category: Traditional Crafts, Performing Arts, Folk Activities, or Traditional Art.
A valid project detail link opens the matching heritage item; an invalid project identifier shows a clear not-found state and a way back to the homepage without displaying unrelated project details.
Every heritage card displays the item's title, brief description, region or province, and category.
Category-browsing navigation from a heritage detail page returns the user to the project list on the homepage.
checklist.bug: The detail-page category link only appends #categories to the current /heritage/:id URL, where no categories section exists, instead of navigating to /#categories.

checklist.content: Images presented for a heritage item are relevant to and consistent with the item's name and description.
checklist.bug: Several generic Unsplash stock photos are unrelated to their associated heritage items; for example, the Suzhou Embroidery gallery includes unrelated imagery.

checklist.content: Users can rotate the panorama through a full 360 degrees and continue to see and interact with hotspots as the view wraps around; zooming does not cause hotspots to be permanently lost.
checklist.bug: The camera yaw is never normalized. After a 360-degree drag, hotspot visibility compares raw angles, so all hotspots disappear until the user rotates all the way back.

checklist.content: The detail-page image gallery lets users select each available image and updates the main image area or its explicit failure state to match the selected image.
Search, filter, and sort selections remain applied after a user opens a heritage detail page and returns to the project list.

instruction: I want a webpage where I can organize my data in a flexible database. I should be able to add entries with different types of fields like text, numbers, dates, and checkboxes. The page should let me switch between viewing my data as a simple table or as cards in a grid layout. I need basic ways to sort entries by any field and filter them to show only what I'm looking for. All changes should appear immediately as I work.Additional features include a quick search bar and the ability to manually adjust the order of entries in both table and card views (sort states are saved automatically). Furthermore, the selection of field types will restrict the subsequent input formats. Field configuration must be completed before importing data; otherwise, the data cannot be parsed correctly due to format mismatches. Meanwhile, the sorting rules for the table and card views are not shared with each other, and sorting criteria need to be reconfigured after switching views.

checklist.content: Users can create an entry with values for configured fields; the new entry appears immediately and remains present after the page is reloaded.
checklist.bug: Entries and other database changes exist only in in-memory component state, so reloading restores the seed data.

checklist.content: Users can add fields and choose text, number, date, or checkbox as each field's type; the new field appears in entry forms and both data views.
Users can enter and save a text string, number, calendar date, and checkbox status for an entry, and the saved values are retained and shown in both data views.
Users can switch between table and card views without changing the current entries or their field values.
Users can sort the current view by any configured field in ascending or descending order; table and card views retain independent sort selections while the user switches between them.
Users can define field-specific filter criteria, view only matching entries, and clear the filters to restore the unfiltered data.
checklist.bug: The app provides free-text search but has no filter control or field-specific filtering logic.

checklist.content: When no field sort is active, users can manually reorder entries in table and card views; each view retains its own manual order while the user switches between them.
A number field accepts valid numeric values and prevents a non-numeric value from being saved as that field's value.
A date field accepts valid calendar dates and prevents an invalid date value from being saved as that field's value.
Sorting changes only the order of entries; it preserves the entry count and every saved field value.
Filtering includes exactly the entries that satisfy the active criteria; clearing the filters restores all entries without modifying or deleting data.
checklist.bug: Filtering is not implemented, so criteria cannot be applied or cleared.

checklist.content: Every entry and each configured field value are displayed consistently in both table and card views, including a clear representation for an empty value.
checklist.bug: Card view promotes the first text field to an unlabeled title and omits it completely when its value is empty, so neither the field nor an empty-value indicator is shown.

checklist.content: Field-type choices are clearly labeled during configuration, and entry forms provide type-appropriate controls for text, number, date, and checkbox fields.
Checkbox values have clearly distinguishable checked and unchecked states in entry forms and both data views.
Quick search returns entries whose text values contain the query case-insensitively, updates the visible result count, and restores all entries when cleared.
Selecting a sort field immediately reorders the visible entries, identifies the active field and direction, and leaves the app usable.
Users can import data after defining a field schema, and the app rejects imported values that do not match the configured field types without corrupting existing data.
checklist.bug: No data-import action or import-processing logic exists, despite the brief's requirement that field configuration precede import.

checklist.content: Quick search matches the field values shown to users, including formatted dates and checkbox states, rather than only internal raw values.
checklist.bug: Search compares raw values, so displayed checkbox labels such as "Yes" and "No" and formatted date text cannot be found by those visible values.

instruction: I want a webpage where I can browse and use text templates created by others. I should be able to view a template library (e.g., resumes, weekly reports, or meeting minutes), select a template, fill in the relevant information through a simple form, and preview the results. I also want to be able to submit my own templates in plain text or Markdown format, which will also appear in the template library. Each template should display basic information such as author and description. New features and constraints: 1. Support for template categorization and multi-dimensional searching, allowing filtering by template type, applicable scenarios, popularity, and update time; the search box supports fuzzy keyword matching and real-time associative suggestions; 2. Support for template favorites, with a favorites list for quick retrieval of frequently used templates; 3. Form filling and generation constraints: set required fields for forms, preventing content generation when required fields are not filled; restrict special characters in input content to avoid formatting errors in the generated text.

checklist.content: Users can browse the template library and see the available templates with their authors and descriptions.
Selecting a template opens its customizable form and template details.
Users can enter values for every field defined by the selected template.
After all required fields are valid, users can preview the generated result with their values substituted into the template.
Users can submit a custom plain-text or Markdown template with a title, description, author, category, scenario, content, and at least one defined field.
After a custom template is successfully submitted, it appears in the current browser's template library and can be selected and used.
Each template card displays its title, author, description, category, scenario, usage count, and update date.

For a built-in Markdown template, filling all required fields produces a preview with every declared placeholder replaced and Markdown headings, emphasis, separators, and line breaks rendered correctly.
Users can filter templates by category and scenario and sort results by popularity, update recency, creation age, or title; the visible result count and order update accordingly.
Search tolerates a small typo in a template keyword and still returns or suggests the intended matching template.
checklist.bug: Search uses case-insensitive substring matching only; entering 'Resme' returns zero results instead of matching 'Professional Resume'.

checklist.content: Users can add or remove a template from favorites and open a favorites-only list.
Within the favorites-only view, users can search and filter their saved templates.
Users can copy the generated result to the clipboard in the selected template's declared format, with visible success feedback.
Fields with a declared format, such as email or date, reject invalid values or keep preview unavailable until the value is valid.
checklist.bug: An invalid email such as 'not-an-email' is accepted, and built-in date-like text fields accept values such as 'not a date'; preview still becomes available.

checklist.content: Custom templates cannot be submitted without a nonblank title, description, author, content, and at least one defined field.
Values entered into template fields reject or neutralize special characters that would alter generated Markdown structure or formatting.
checklist.bug: Validation blocks only a limited character set and permits Markdown metacharacters such as #, *, and _. Entering '# Unexpected Heading' in a textarea renders an unintended level-one heading in the preview.

checklist.content: The preview remains unavailable until every required field of the selected template has a nonblank, valid value.
Typing at least two matching characters shows real-time suggestions; choosing a suggestion fills the search and narrows the library to matching templates.
Search queries, category and scenario filters, favorites-only mode, and sort choices update the visible results and count without a reload.
When required selected-template fields are empty, the UI lists the missing fields and keeps preview unavailable.
Favoriting or unfavoriting a template provides immediate visual feedback and updates the favorites count and list.
Valid plain-text templates preview as preserved text, and valid Markdown templates render expected Markdown after field substitution.
Submitting a valid custom template immediately updates the library and visible result count without a reload.

A custom template can be submitted only when every declared dynamic field maps to a placeholder in its content and every content placeholder maps to a declared field; generated previews contain no unresolved placeholders.
checklist.bug: Submission performs no field-to-placeholder validation. A template defining {{name}} but containing {{missing}} is accepted, and its preview still shows 'Hello {{missing}}' after Name is filled.

checklist.content: Favorites and custom templates remain available after reloading the app in the same browser.
Every field defined for a custom template remains independently fillable; duplicate labels are rejected or disambiguated before submission.
checklist.bug: Duplicate labels are accepted and normalized to the same field identifier. Two fields labelled 'Name' both become {{name}}, producing duplicate keys and shared form state rather than independent values.

instruction: I want to create a webpage that implements a purely front-end-based job competency modeling and simulation system. HR professionals can search for competency models by job name or keywords, and the page will display a list of results and access detailed information. On the details page, the system needs to represent the competency model as a directed weighted graph structure, with nodes representing competencies and edges representing dependencies or reinforcement relationships. Users can directly drag and drop to adjust competency levels, modify weights, or temporarily enable/disable certain competencies. The page needs to recalculate competency coverage, critical paths, and risk competency gaps in real time after each structural change, and immediately alert users to potential problems. The system should provide a general job competency model template library, allowing HR professionals to quickly build models and save custom templates. It should also support scenario-based simulations for recruitment, training, and promotion, simulating the impact of model adjustments under different scenarios.

checklist.content: Searching by a case-insensitive job-title, keyword, or description fragment returns exactly the matching competency models; an optional department filter further narrows the results, and no matches produce a clear empty state.
Selecting a model from the search results opens the corresponding detail editor with the matching job title, summary metrics, and competency graph.
Users can drag competency nodes to rearrange the graph layout while existing directed relationships remain attached to the correct competencies and their meaning does not change.
Users can change the weight of a competency relationship, after which the displayed relationship weight, its visual emphasis, and any dependent analysis update immediately.
checklist.bug: Relationship weights are read-only: the graph displays edge labels and weighted strokes, but no control or handler edits model.edges; the visible weight sliders edit competency weights instead.

checklist.content: Users can disable and later re-enable a competency; the node and its relationships clearly show the disabled state, disabled competencies are excluded from coverage, gap, and critical-path calculations, and repeated toggles act on the current state.
checklist.bug: React Flow keeps stale node data. Disabling changes parent metrics but leaves the switch checked and the node and edges active-looking; clicking again calls the original callback and cannot re-enable it. The critical-path calculation can also re-add a disabled competency through a dependency edge.

checklist.content: Users can browse the template library and compare each available job-role template by its role, department, competency count, relationship count, and representative keywords.
Applying a template replaces the edited model consistently, so the title, metrics, competency graph, relationships, and scenario-adjustment categories all represent the selected template.
checklist.bug: Applying a template updates the model title, metrics, and scenario counts, but CompetencyGraph's useNodesState/useEdgesState values are initialized only once, so the previous template's graph remains visible.

checklist.content: Users can save the current edited model as a custom template with a name and description, then retrieve the same configuration from a My Templates collection after leaving and returning.
checklist.bug: Save Current only shows a success toast. There is no naming or description workflow, custom-template state or storage, or My Templates collection.

checklist.content: Users can switch among Recruitment, Training, and Promotion simulation scenarios, and the scenario description and category adjustments update to match the selected scenario.

Users can choose category-level competency and weight adjustments for a scenario, run the simulation to update coverage, average level, critical-path and risk-gap outputs, and reset the model to its original state.
After editing a model, users can save and later restore the same levels, weights, and enabled states after leaving and reopening the model or reloading the app.
checklist.bug: Save only reports success through a toast. Reopening the model or reloading reconstructs it from static seed data and loses all edits.

checklist.content: Direct edits and scenario simulations keep every competency level within 1 to 5 and every competency weight within the supported 10% to 100% range.
Changing an enabled competency's level or weight, or changing which competencies are enabled, immediately updates the displayed coverage percentage and progress indicator without a reload.

The detail editor presents the current model as an interactive directed weighted graph: nodes identify competencies, arrowed connections identify dependency or reinforcement relationships, relationship weights are visible, and users can pan, zoom, and rearrange the view.

After a relevant competency-weight or enabled-state change, the critical-path summary and graph highlighting recalculate immediately, form a valid path through enabled competencies, and agree with each other.
checklist.bug: The calculation selects high-weight competencies and some inbound dependencies rather than computing a graph path, can include a disabled dependency, and the graph's stale React Flow state prevents updated node and edge highlighting from being rendered.

checklist.content: Lowering an enabled high-weight competency below the recommended level immediately creates a risk-gap warning naming that competency; resolving the level or disabling the competency clears it.
When one or more risk competency gaps are detected, the app prominently displays a text-and-icon alert near the summary metrics that names the affected competencies and suggests corrective action.

The initially selected simulation scenario is fully initialized: its default adjustments are visible and running it without first switching tabs applies those adjustments and changes the corresponding model outputs.
checklist.bug: The Recruitment tab is selected initially, but adjustments starts as an empty object and defaults are populated only by a tab-change handler. Running the initial scenario makes no model change while still showing a misleading Simulation Applied success toast.

checklist.content: After any competency level, weight, or enabled-state edit, the graph control displays the current value or state, its Gap and Critical indicators agree with the summary analysis, and a subsequent edit starts from that current state.
checklist.bug: CompetencyGraph initializes React Flow node state once and never synchronizes it with changed model props. Metrics and alerts update, but node labels, sliders, switches, and Gap/Critical badges remain stale; later edits can therefore overwrite newer state with old values.
